The instant appeal preferred under Section 21(4) of the National Investigation Agency Act, 2008 is directed against the order dated 05.10.2023 passed in Misc. Cri. Application No.467 of 2023 by the Addl. Sessions Judge-I-Cum-Special Judge, POCSO, Simdega, in connection with Spl. POCSO Case No.13 of 2023, arising out Simdega A.H.T.U. P.S. Case No.05 of 2022, corresponding to G.R.
No.159 of 2023 registered under Sections 363, 370(4), 376 and 34 of the IPC, Sections 75 and 81 of the Juvenile Justice Act and Sections 4 and 8 of the POCSO Act, whereby and whereunder, the prayer for regular bail of the appellant has been rejected.
2. It has been contended on behalf of the appellant that it is a case where the appellant has falsely been implicated in the case, since, even no incriminating material has been surfaced in course of investigation.
3. It has further been submitted that even though, there is no specific attributability said to have been committed by the appellant even then, he is languishing in judicial custody since 08.02.2023.

sentences.text: Therefore, the learned Court, while considering the prayer for bail of the appellant ought to have considered these aspects of the matter but having not done so, the order impugned needs to be interfered with.
5. While, on the other hand, learned APP appearing for the respondent-State has vehemently opposed the prayer for regular bail.
6. The ground has been taken by referring the imputation of allegation against the appellant for trafficking of the victim on allurement of providing good job in Delhi.
7. The said victim, girl was subsequently handed over to this appellant.

8. It has also come that the appellant subsequent thereto had deployed her in a Kothi in Merrut where the work was taken from her without making any money and even she was not allowed to talk with her family member.
9. It has also come that in absence of his wife, the appellant used to commit rape upon her.
Even the dead foetus was also found and the sample of the same was sent to the FSL, which is awaiting.

10. Learned APP appearing for the State-respondent, based upon the aforesaid ground has submitted that it is not a fit case where the benefit of regular bail is to be granted by interfering with the order impugned dated 05.10.2023.

11. We have heard the learned counsel for the parties and perused the finding recorded by the learned Court in the impugned order dated 05.10.2023.
12.

It is evident from the finding recorded by the learned Court as available in the impugned order,
wherein, the reason for rejecting the prayer for regular bail has been referred that:-
(i) The victim girl in the year 2019 was trafficked by her cousin brother, namely,
Somaru on allurement of providing good job and taken her to Delhi.
In Delhi, she was handed over by Somaru (cousin of the victim) to Rajendra Nayak, the appellant herein.
(ii) The petitioner, appellant herein had deployed her in a Kothi in Merrut.
(iii) She worked as maid servant there for one year and subsequently, she was brought to his house and kept there for one month.
(iv) There was allegation of assault upon the appellant and his wife as also they did not allow her to talk with her family members.
(v) It has also come against the appellant that in absence of his wife, he used to commit rape upon her, the victim.

sentences.text: 13. Learned court, while considering the prayer for regular bail has taken all these grounds and come to the conclusion that it is not a fit case to grant bail in favour of the petitioner, the appellant herein.
14. We, on consideration of the reason, basis upon which, the learned court has rejected the prayer for regular bail, therefore, are of the view that the order impugned requires no interference.
15. Accordingly, the instant appeal is dismissed.

(Sujit Narayan Prasad, J.) (Pradeep Kumar Srivastava, J.) Rohit/-
